evidence.observation: | `reference_populations`, sample populations | none in the ontology; mappings are layer 1 | out of scope |

"Every model element has exactly one disposition ... `native` ... `requires` ... `extension` ... or `refused`" and "An element without a disposition is an internal error (exit 70), not a quiet omission." (Context: src/gnd/schema/orm-meta.schema.json line 76 defines top-level "reference_populations", so it is a real model element.)

concerns.recommendation: Give populations one of the four dispositions: `extension`, or `refused` with a closed reason code such as `population:out-of-scope`. Make the census test cover populations. Then state whether the predicate-5 `gnd diff` round trip compares populations.
concerns.title: Populations get 'out of scope', which is not a disposition, so they are lost silently or the export exits 70

evidence.observation: "A population that violates a constraint shows the same verdict under GND's checker and under the formula's meaning. This is shown by differential cases, one per exported constraint kind (OS2-C2)."
"the converter emits **no `require`**"; OS2: "Each formula is checked by `OssieParser` in the oracle lane, and by GND's own grammar check". Both are parse checks only, and no evaluator is named.

concerns.recommendation: Name the evaluator for 'the formula's meaning'. That could be an independent interpreter of the Ossie formula AST built from ontology.md's semantics and kept separate from pyrel_rules, or hand-written expected verdicts per case. Otherwise, narrow predicate 4 to parse-acceptance plus hand-reviewed semantic cases, so that it can actually fail.
concerns.title: Predicate 4's semantic-equivalence check has no evaluator independent of GND

evidence.observation: "the document carries the model's identity digest (OS1-C3)"
"If it is not admitted, the fallback is a sidecar `FILE.gnd.json` bound by digest to the document (OD2). Content: ... plus the model identity digest."

concerns.recommendation: Say where the digest lives when E1 rejects custom_extensions, for example in a schema-admitted field such as a description or IRI. Otherwise make predicate 2 conditional on OD2's outcome, and say that under the sidecar route the digest is in the sidecar.
concerns.title: Predicate 2 may not be satisfiable under the OD2 sidecar fallback

evidence.observation: "Where the converter skips a construct, the skip is recorded in the loss report as a consumer limitation" and "the corresponding consumer-limitation row in the loss report goes away"

"`ossie_relationalai` run only in the opt-in `ossie_oracle` lane ... never GND runtime dependencies". The loss report has only four dispositions: "`native` ... `requires` ... `extension` ... `refused`".

concerns.recommendation: Keep the consumer-limitation record separate from the `gnd export ossie` loss report, for example as an OS4 lane artifact or a pinned static table keyed by converter commit. Then define its schema, so the runtime report stays deterministic and free of any converter dependency.
concerns.title: Consumer-limitation rows come from the opt-in lane but are placed in the runtime loss report

evidence.observation: "a branch in a fork, with upstream tests passing locally at the pin ...; then an upstream PR, posted only after the owner approves its exact title and body."

concerns.recommendation: Add a separate owner gate before the fork is created or any branch is pushed to a public remote. Alternatively, keep the branch local until the PR go-ahead, because publishing a public fork is already outward-facing.
concerns.title: Only the PR text is gated; creating the fork and pushing the branch publicly are not

evidence.observation: "then GND admission, then the extension digest. The order is pinned by a source-order assertion (OS3-C2)."
"Import verifies the digest before using any of it (rule 3)."

concerns.recommendation: Fix one order. Either verify the extension's binding digest before GND admission consumes extension content (role order, Duration meaning, modality), or state that admission runs only on the native projection, followed by a second admission after the verified extension is merged.
concerns.title: The import validation order contradicts 'verify the digest before using' the extension

evidence.observation: "OS6-C2, for every OS2 constraint kind the converter now renders, GND's OS4 lane observes a `require`"
"Every compliance sentence names the Ossie spec version and the two pinned commits. A re-pin is its own owner-gated change."

concerns.recommendation: State that OS6-C2 runs the OS4 lane against a fork commit. Record that commit separately from the R7 compliance pin, and keep the published loss report on the 83ddc294 converter unless an owner-gated re-pin happens.
concerns.title: OS6-C2 needs the OS4 lane to run against an unpinned fork converter, which conflicts with R7

evidence.observation: "| `independent`, `storage`, `description`, `provenance` | ... | native + extension |" and fact types: "native; roles reordered ... with the original GND order kept in the extension"
"Every model element has exactly one disposition"

concerns.recommendation: Define what counts as an element for the disposition walk, for example per attribute or JSON pointer. Without that, 'native + extension' rows break 'exactly one', and the census test cannot check uniqueness.
concerns.title: The mapping gives some elements two dispositions, but predicate 3 says exactly one

evidence.observation: "OS4 → {OS5, OS6} → close" vs "It does not block the close: if the PR is still open at close, its state is recorded as a carryover."
Predicate 9 requires the PR to have been "opened upstream", while §6 says "Upstream PR (OS6) is rejected or stalls | not a close criterion".

concerns.recommendation: State plainly that close requires the PR to have been opened, with merge not required, and say what happens if the owner declines to approve the PR text. Align the dependency arrow and the §6 wording with that.
concerns.title: Whether OS6 gates close is stated inconsistently

evidence.observation: "The owner ruled OD0–OD7 on 2026-11-10" vs §1.4 "rulings OD0–OD8 (§10)". §10 also holds the OD8 ruling and says OD3 is "not ruled separately".

concerns.recommendation: Change the status line to OD0–OD8 and note that OD3 follows from OD1.
concerns.title: The status line says OD0–OD7, but OD8 is also ruled

evidence.observation: "OS0 → OS1 → {OS2, OS3} → OS4" vs "OS4 needs OS1, and uses OS2 output where available."

concerns.recommendation: Draw the graph to match the prose: OS4 depends on OS1 only, OS2 is a soft input, and OS3 is not a prerequisite.
concerns.title: The phase arrow makes OS3 a prerequisite of OS4, but the prose says it is not

response.summary: The plan is well structured. Credential-free gates, the owner gate on the upstream PR text, and the pinning are handled well. Two problems are blocking. First, the mapping marks reference/sample populations as 'out of scope', which is not one of the four dispositions predicate 3 requires, so a real metaschema element is silently lost. Second, predicate 4's differential check has no independent evaluator for 'the formula's meaning'. The hardening concerns are: the identity digest under the sidecar fallback, consumer-limitation rows in a runtime loss report, an ungated public fork push, the import digest order, an unpinned fork converter in OS6-C2, and 'native + extension' rows that conflict with 'exactly one disposition'. A few consistency gaps remain around OS6 and close, and the OD numbering in the status line.
